sentences.text: The thesis's central premise holds and is strengthening: Data Center growth on a year earlier rose to +116.6%. The segment supplied +102.5 percentage points of the +105.9% total growth, so the overweight case rests almost entirely on one line of business.

The margin leg adds little to that case. Gross margin is 0.2 percentage points below where it was eight quarters ago, and the filing calls it approximately flat sequentially, so any earnings upside into the report has to come from revenue rather than margin.

The risk claims are true as disclosures, but none yet shows in the numbers. The one computable China test runs against the export-control claim by +97.7 points, and the company's own concentration and supplier warnings sit beside a quarter of unbroken growth.

The record ends before the decision's horizon. The CEO resigned effective immediately in an 8-K filed after the newest 10-Q, and none of the financial evidence can weigh what that means for the next report.
The quality of the growth carries two cautions the bullish claims do not address. Receivable days rose to 59.6 from 54.1, and inventory days rose to 119.3 from 105.6.
A careful investor would want three things from the next filing: whether quarterly revenue stays above $96.22B, whether receivable days stop climbing, and how the leadership transition is disclosed.
The year-over-year margin test passes with room of only 1.27x a typical move, and it held in just 12 of 20 past readings, so the expansion reading is fragile on its own history.
The comparison base is depressed by the prior year's $4.5 billion H20 charge. On a full-year basis the claim fails, by -3.9 points, which makes the expansion a recovery rather than a new gain.
Sequentially the gain is +0.04 points, which the filing itself describes as approximately flat, so nothing in the record backs margin as a source of upside into the report.

Revenue rose in each of the last 8 quarters, at a compound +15.7% a quarter. Year-over-year growth also sped up by 20.6 percentage points in the newest quarter, so the trend into the report is accelerating rather than fading.
Data Center is outgrowing the company and its share rose to 92.5% from 87.9%, so the line the thesis depends on is gaining weight, not losing it.
Customer concentration is not visibly intensifying. Q2 FY2027 names one direct customer at 16%, against three in Q1 at 21%, 17% and 16%, which softens the concentration risk.
The CEO's immediate resignation, with the CFO as interim CEO, is an execution risk landing squarely in the holding period, and the record has no evidence to size it.
Receivables grew +126.8% against revenue growth of +105.9%, a result that runs against what the growth claim implies. It raises the question of how much of the growth has turned into cash.

On the annual basis, Data Center growth slowed by 74.2 percentage points, and the filing warns that faster product transitions may make revenue volatile. With one segment at 92.5% of revenue, any stumble in it hits the whole company.
Quarterly revenue comes in above $96.22B.
Gross margin holds at or above 75.0%.
Receivable days stay at or below 59.6.
Quarterly revenue falls below $96.22B, breaking the run of sequential rises.
Receivable days rise above 59.6 while inventory days rise above 119.3.
Quarterly gross margin falls below 72.4%, so the year-over-year test fails.
A filing discloses an inventory or purchase-obligation charge like the $4.5 billion H20 charge.
A further Item 5.02 8-K discloses additional leadership change following the CEO's resignation.
